title: What transfers from a source into Coq?
method: Qualitative claim-level comparison added after the implementations. Preserve original source-target groups; G/T labels are retrospective groupings. No success percentages, tier scores or effort-normalized comparisons are calculated.
limits: All five sources remain F3 pilots with source-level determinations withheld.
Source-target groups differ in size and centrality; they are not interchangeable units in a rate.
One researcher assessed the mappings. Grice/Tarski are existing pilots, not held-out or independent replications.
Abstract parameters are not automatically semantic gaps; adding a conclusion-bearing constraint is different from choosing a carrier type.
Encoding robustness is untested for every profile. Existing parameter/boundary checks are reported separately.
Topic, scope, investigator choices and unmeasured effort confound any tier comparison; more formal notation alone would only restate the rubric.

profiles.label: Derrida 1972
profiles.grouping: D1–D6 retained from the pre-implementation inventory
profiles.source_supplies: Conceptual distinctions between repeatable form, occurrence, context, origin and structural possibility.
profiles.coverage: Selected distinctions are illustrated; the central non-saturation thesis is not stated or proved.
profiles.semantic_additions: An inductive context syntax, exact form equality, a chosen interpreter and a two-world modal model. Ignoring producer metadata is our choice.
profiles.ordinary_parameters: Token/form/origin carriers in the conditional information-loss lemma are legitimate abstraction parameters; no origin detector is required.
profiles.preservation: Agrammaticality-as-example and possible-failure/success distinctions are represented. These are constructed examples, not predictions derived from the whole argument.
profiles.boundary_checks: Within-model checks separate same form from same effect, syntactic infinity from semantic variation, and form-only from richer evidence.
profiles.robustness_note: No alternative source-faithful account of contextual identity or interpretation has been implemented.

targets.source_claim: Readability/iterability can outlast a particular producer's presence.
targets.established: A modeled occurrence is readable with producer metadata absent.
targets.limit: Metadata independence is stipulated; neither universal readability nor universal intention-independence follows.

targets.source_claim: Detachment and citational graft; agrammaticality can itself be exemplified.
targets.established: The worked contrast and unbounded quotation syntax have checked properties.
targets.limit: The syntax and interpretation are added, not a derivation of the philosophical claim.

targets.source_claim: Citability does not imply validity outside context.
targets.established: Context cannot be erased from this interpreter; infinitely many quotes can keep one effect.
targets.limit: These countermodels delimit inferences; they do not establish semantic non-saturation.

targets.source_claim: Repeatable signature form differs from a singular occurrence/origin.
targets.established: Equal observed forms with different origins prevent correct form-only decoding of both.
targets.limit: The collision premises and exact form criterion are supplied; richer authentication is not excluded.

targets.source_claim: Possibility of failure coexists with successful performances.
targets.established: A two-world model separates necessary possible failure from every actual performance failing.
targets.limit: The accessibility relation is added, not a formal definition of Derrida's structural possibility.

targets.source_claim: Universal non-saturation, dissemination and the philosophical critique.
targets.established: No corresponding mathematical statement established.
targets.limit: Outside this signature, not proved impossible, false or inconsistent.

profiles.label: Austin 1962
profiles.grouping: A1–A7 retained from the pre-implementation inventory
profiles.source_supplies: Six provisional necessary conditions, conditional Gamma applicability, overlapping failures and worked speech-act examples.
profiles.coverage: The taxonomy is represented and necessary-condition consequences checked; full felicity is not decided.
profiles.semantic_additions: Partial Boolean observations, a strict two-event recognizer and assigned observations/achievement for worked cases.
profiles.ordinary_parameters: Whether a procedure is accepted or an intention sincere can legitimately remain an input. Lack of an automatic social-fact detector is not a formalization failure.
profiles.preservation: Misfire versus abuse, overlapping failures and incidental effects are retained. Promise achievement is supplied, not derived from passing the checklist.
profiles.boundary_checks: Unknown observations are not success; extra requirements can defeat sufficiency; Gamma failure need not be incomplete execution.
profiles.robustness_note: Information-refinement and example tests are within one representation, not comparisons of alternative felicity encodings.

targets.source_claim: Provisional necessary conditions; Gamma clauses apply where required.
targets.established: Six labels and conditional applicability are represented; failed necessary conditions exclude felicity given a necessity premise.
targets.limit: Diagnostic soundness is relative to assigned observations; the taxonomy is not established as a sufficient test.

targets.source_claim: Misfire blocks the intended act, not every incidental effect; abuse can accompany achievement.
targets.established: The necessity implication is explicit; bottle-breaking and later breach are separate coordinates.
targets.limit: Achievement is not derived from A/B success, and the examples assign rather than discover institutional facts.

targets.source_claim: An insincere promise is still a promise.
targets.established: The example consistently combines supplied achievement with a Gamma1 failure.
targets.limit: Achievement is set to True for the example. The proof checks the representation, not an independent prediction.

targets.source_claim: A bet needs acceptance; correct and complete execution differ.
targets.established: An added strict recognizer accepts exactly an isolated offer followed by acceptance.
targets.limit: Not a grammar of all procedures; later events lie outside this recognizer and do not establish that bets are undone.

targets.source_claim: Failures can coexist and classifications may overlap.
targets.established: The report retains all failed labels, including simultaneous A2 and Gamma1.
targets.limit: Classification of ambiguous social cases remains an input, not a tested judgment.

targets.source_claim: Exclusions, vague applicability and procedural laxness limit the checklist.
targets.established: Unknown observations are separated from success; a further unmet requirement defeats checklist sufficiency.
targets.limit: The countermodel is elementary; real exclusions, uptake and laxness are not modeled generally.

targets.source_claim: Sincere belief and factual correctness differ.
targets.established: A two-coordinate example separates content truth from speaker belief.
targets.limit: No general semantics of assertion or account of Moore's paradox is established.

profiles.label: Horn 1984
profiles.grouping: H1–H6 retained from the pre-implementation inventory
profiles.source_supplies: Regimented Q/R principles, weaker/stronger entailment relationships, cancellation patterns and a qualified division of pragmatic labor.
profiles.coverage: Some source-linked logical relationships are proved directly; the pragmatic interpreter remains a conditional reconstruction.
profiles.semantic_additions: Accessible-world knowledge, a competence premise for negative truth, binary stereotypes, exact common extensions and Boolean default/counterpart flags.
profiles.ordinary_parameters: Worlds, literal propositions, relevance and alternative availability are not defects merely because supplied. Specific stereotype/default choices still need source justification.
profiles.preservation: Numeral cancellation and descriptive-negation distinctions are checked; the direct/indirect causative split is an assigned illustrative case.
profiles.boundary_checks: Ignorance can coexist with stronger truth; disabling defaults or counterpart availability changes the interpreter's readings.
profiles.robustness_note: Parameter withdrawal tests do not compare alternative accounts of stereotypes, markedness or Q/R competition.

targets.source_claim: Relevant non-use of an available stronger form licenses ignorance under Q observance.
targets.established: Non-use implies not knowing the stronger content given the norm; a countermodel separates ignorance from actual falsity.
targets.limit: Norm observance is a premise. Competence and actual-world accessibility are added only for the stronger negative-truth result.

targets.source_claim: Q upper-bounding and R enrichment can compete and be cancelled.
targets.established: The two logical contents are incompatible; cancellation can preserve literal content.
targets.limit: The contradiction lemma intentionally has inconsistent joint premises. Actual contextual default selection is not derived.

targets.source_claim: Descriptive negation differs from cancelling pragmatic enrichment.
targets.established: If S entails W, not-W entails not-S; numeral exactness and stronger-continuation cancellation are checked.
targets.limit: The empirical ban on R-cancelling interpretations of negated utterances is not established by the logic.

targets.source_claim: An available unmarked counterpart supports a marked/non-stereotypical division of labor.
targets.established: A supplied binary stereotype partitions a common extension under the chosen ordinary/counterpart flags; enumeration is exact.
targets.limit: The acceptance rule is our implementation. Its exhaustive binary partition is not independently validated as a universal linguistic prediction.

targets.source_claim: Causatives illustrate the division, but not every shorter synonym is a corresponding alternative.
targets.established: The chosen direct/indirect example changes when counterpart availability is withdrawn.
targets.limit: Correspondence, literal extension and stereotype are supplied; no universal synonym-blocking law follows.

targets.source_claim: Empirical/historical generalizations and general Q/R weighting.
targets.established: No general weighting, learned-stereotype or diachrony result established.
targets.limit: Later sections were outside the reading scope; no impossibility claim.

profiles.label: Grice 1975
profiles.grouping: G1–G4 are retrospective labels for the existing narrative inventory, not preregistered atomic claims
profiles.source_supplies: Three conditions on conversational implicature, the garage example, and cancellation/non-entailment diagnostics.
profiles.coverage: A conditional constraint representation is checked; the garage belief is not independently inferred from the maxims.
profiles.semantic_additions: The garage compatibility predicate is defined to equal the desired belief predicate; presumed cooperation and recognizability are set for that example.
profiles.ordinary_parameters: Belief states and context relations may be abstract. Equating compatibility with the target conclusion is a substantive example choice, not mere abstraction.
profiles.preservation: Opting out blocks this derivation and literal truth is separated from world usability; garage relevance is stipulated.
profiles.boundary_checks: Cooperation withdrawal and a belief/world-fact countercase are checked within the chosen constraint model.
profiles.robustness_note: No alternative account of contextual compatibility or calculability is compared.

targets.source_claim: Three conditions for conversational implicature.
targets.established: The licensed belief follows from the represented conditions and a compatible belief state.
targets.limit: The conclusion is already required of every compatible state by calculable; no mechanism discovers that constraint.

targets.source_claim: The garage reply supports belief in possible usability.
targets.established: The example satisfies the supplied compatibility/recognizability conditions.
targets.limit: Compatibility is defined as the desired belief. This is not an independent derivation from the maxims.

targets.source_claim: Cancellation and non-entailment distinguish implicature from what is said.
targets.established: Opt-out blocks this conditional derivation while literal content can remain true; inferred belief does not force world fact.
targets.limit: These test cases do not characterize every cancellation mechanism or all conversational implicatures.

targets.source_claim: General contextual relevance and recognizable reasoning.
targets.established: No general relevance, mutual-recognition or raw-language inference procedure established.
targets.limit: Not having an automatic procedure is not by itself an impossibility of formalizing the conditions.

profiles.label: Tarski 1944
profiles.grouping: T1–T4 are retrospective labels for the existing narrative inventory, not preregistered atomic claims
profiles.source_supplies: Object/metalanguage separation, an outline of recursive satisfaction and truth via assignments, and Convention T as an adequacy schema.
profiles.coverage: A restricted first-order construction supports structural metatheorems and T-instances; no unrestricted truth theory is claimed.
profiles.semantic_additions: A chosen unary-predicate language with variables, snow, conjunction, negation and universal quantification; a nonempty domain via a named snow object; constructive metatheory.
profiles.ordinary_parameters: The domain and predicate interpretations are legitimate model parameters, not missing algorithms. Restricting the language and not proving classical bivalence must still be disclosed.
profiles.preservation: The snow instance and closed contradiction test are checked; assignment invariance supports language-specific T-equivalences.
profiles.boundary_checks: Free-variable agreement is sufficient for satisfaction invariance across arbitrary assignments in this syntax; contradiction has no satisfying assignment.
profiles.robustness_note: A parametric structural theorem is stronger than one finite example, but no alternate syntax or classical metatheory is compared.

targets.source_claim: Recursive satisfaction separates object language from metalanguage.
targets.established: Satisfaction is recursive for the chosen language; dependence only on free variables is proved structurally.
targets.limit: A specific fragment and nonempty domain are chosen; no internal truth predicate is added.

targets.source_claim: Convention T is an adequacy schema, not a substitute truth definition.
targets.established: Closed assignment invariance yields T-equivalences after recursive satisfaction is defined.
targets.limit: These are language-specific instances, not truth for Coq or unrestricted natural language.

targets.source_claim: The construction should handle the snow example and exclude contradiction.
targets.established: The snow equivalence and absence of satisfying assignments for contradiction are checked.
targets.limit: The contradiction test is a new integrity check, not an independent empirical prediction or a proof of bivalence.

targets.source_claim: Limits of the attempt: no self-applicable truth, undefinability proof or classical bivalence result.
targets.established: No diagonal lemma, undefinability theorem or classical bivalence result established.
targets.limit: These omissions are not counted as refutations and are not licensed by the bounded construction.
